exposure: maternal antibiotic use during gestation and delivery
outcome: antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in meconium and stool samples
alpha diversity of microbiota and resistome
cohort: A subset of 30 preterm infants from the Routine Early Antibiotic Use in Symptomatic Preterm Neonates study, whose meconium and subsequent stool samples were analyzed.
finding: All preterm infants exhibited a high prevalence of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), and postnatal antibiotic exposure increased beta-lactam/tetracycline resistance, altered bacterial resistance mechanisms, and reduced microbial and resistome alpha diversity.
